actions.reason: C0001 has a coherent RNA-defined identity with strong, FDR-significant pathway enrichment (e.g., downregulated adipogenesis, upregulated allograft rejection) and large effect sizes. WXS and CNV findings are concordant but not significant after correction, yet they do not contradict the RNA signal. Technical confounders are not significant, and known-label overlap is low. Structural metrics show stable internal structure (high ARI, low PAC) despite weak global silhouettes, and no positive evidence supports Split or Merge. Retaining C0001 for downstream validation is better supported than Drop.

C0002 lacks coherent positive identity evidence: RNA shows no significant pathway enrichment, WXS and CNV findings are not significant after FDR correction, and effect sizes are modest. Cross-modal support is weak with near-zero silhouettes and unstable internal structure (low ARI, high PAC). Technical confounders are not significant, but the absence of a meaningful biological or phenotypic identity makes the set insufficiently defensible. No positive structural evidence supports Split or Merge, and no extra evidence is available to resolve the uncertainty. Dropping C0002 is better supported than Accept.

C0003 has a coherent RNA-defined identity with strong, FDR-significant pathway enrichment (e.g., upregulated heme metabolism, downregulated allograft rejection) and large effect sizes, supported by significant CNV differences (e.g., lower chr20q, chr7p, CDKN2A loss). WXS BAP1 depletion is concordant but not significant after correction. Technical confounders are not significant, and known-label overlap is low. Structural metrics show moderate internal stability (ARI 0.60, PAC 0.53) and RNA provides the strongest boundary separation. No positive evidence supports Split or Merge. Retaining C0003 for downstream validation is better supported than Drop.
